extracted.subtask_description: Practical precepts for composing poetry and plays: guidance on unity, diction, metre, characterization, dramatic structure, chorus use, and the poet's moral and artistic preparation. Aimed at poets/dramatists crafting works in the classical tradition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency and unity of composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The work should be 'of a piece from end to end' — not a jumble of incoherent, dream-like forms where 'nought is of a piece from end to end.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unnatural or absurd unions of incongruent elements (e.g., mixing lamb with tiger, dolphin in a forest). Ensure beginning, middle, and end agree; make the whole homogeneous rather than a patchwork. Example antipattern: 'unions of lamb with tiger, snake with bird.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate scope of subject to poet's powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Ponder whether the subject you hope to lift is equal to your powers; don't attempt themes 'whose weight would make my powers give way.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose themes you can handle with dignity and strength. If the chosen theme is too great, either lower the ambition or develop powers further; avoid attempting subjects that result in bombast or collapse under their own weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful selection and innovation in diction
rubrics_metrics.description: In words be cautious and select; pick out what to include and what to reject. A good poet can make an old word new; new words are tolerable if modest and derived from Greek.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prune redundance, improve harshnesses by refinement, and avoid careless or unworthy words. Coined words should flow naturally (preferably from Greek) and be used modestly; don't capriciously forbid useful innovations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid extremes: bombast and obscurity
rubrics_metrics.description: Attempts at grandeur can lapse into bombast; striving for terseness can make verse obscure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steer a middle course—be neither needlessly ornate nor obscurely compressed. Antipatterns: 'who aims at grandeur into bombast falls' and 'I prove obscure in trying to be terse.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoughtful planning and clear arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: Ponder your subject often; consider if it's suitable; 'say just now what should just now be said' and put off other matters for later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure your piece so that language and arrangement suit the subject. Plan through repeated consideration and avoid ad hoc piling-on of unrelated material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate metre for theme
rubrics_metrics.description: Different metres suit different themes: 'For metres, Homer shows you how to write heroic deeds,' elegiac was for complaints or love, Archilochus' iambics for biting discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match metre to subject and genre. Learn the properties of metres (e.g., iambic trimeter's pattern and spondaic substitutions) and avoid forcing an unsuitable metre onto a topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect genre-specific proprieties
rubrics_metrics.description: Each genre has its place and vehicle; 'A comic subject steadily declines / To be related in high tragic lines.' Tragedy and comedy have distinct terms and tones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain the proper stylistic register for the genre; don't make the Thyestean feast the subject of comic strains. Antipatterns: mixing comic meters with high tragic subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show action and feeling rather than merely tell
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature forms our spirits to receive impressions; 'Words follow looks' — actors should first show emotion (looks, gestures) which words then follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On stage, express feeling through action and physiognomy—let the visible and enacted precede verbal explanation. Example: a hero should weep or enact sorrow before expecting the audience's tears.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character-appropriate diction and register
rubrics_metrics.description: Gods, heroes, youths, ladies, nurses, country folk, and foreigners each require a distinct style: 'Lady and nurse a different language crave... each has his own style.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign vocabulary, rhythm, and sentence patterns appropriate to social rank, age, nationality, and role. Avoid letting a god speak like a common hero or vice versa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency in character construction
rubrics_metrics.description: If inventing an original character, 'see it be wrought on one consistent plan, / And end the same creation it began.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make novel characters internally coherent across the work; avoid contradictions in temperament or behavior. Antipattern: characters who 'careering and careering still' change unpredictably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer faithful adaptation over gratuitous alteration
rubrics_metrics.description: Better to turn the Iliad into a play and carve acts and scenes than to alter facts and characters and tell a known tale strangely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When working with familiar myths or histories, preserve core facts unless you have clear artistic reasons and precautions for change; avoid unnecessary novelty that undermines plausibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Begin at an effective point (avoid diffuse openings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't 'open like the cyclic, with a burst' that rehearses wide background; better to 'hurry to the crisis' or enter at ease where action matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start near the point of interest; avoid long, diffuse preludes that announce everything and produce little effect (antipattern: 'The mountain labours, and a mouse is born').

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-reliance on spectacle and foreign finery
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive pomp—chariots, ships, exotic animals—dazzles eyes while drowning the voice of the poet; spectacle should not substitute for art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let visual pageantry supplant coherent plot, character, and language. The crowd applauds finery, but the discerning critic prizes literary skill. Antipattern: plays kept for hours with pageants that mask poor writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-act structure for plays
rubrics_metrics.description: A play should have five acts, 'nor more nor fewer.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure dramatic works into five acts for proper development and pacing; avoid arbitrary expansion or contraction of dramatic arc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit deus ex machina and excessive interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Bring in no god save as a last resource.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use divine intervention only if dramatically necessary and as a final device; relying on gods to resolve plots weakens artistic integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict multi-speaker clusters
rubrics_metrics.description: Nor make four speakers join in the discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid confusion and cacophony onstage by limiting the number of simultaneous speakers in debate scenes; keep clarity of dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chorus should sustain the actor and be relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: An actor's part the chorus should sustain... whatever they chant between acts should be apt, appropriate, relevant; they should give sage counsel, temper wrath, conceal secrets, and implore the gods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign the chorus supportive, plot-reinforcing, and moralizing functions rather than distracting ones. Their interludes must relate to the action and advance themes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate musical accompaniment and chorus modesty
rubrics_metrics.description: The flute was used to lend the chorus aid: simple, slight, moderately loud, fit for a not-too-large crowd; avoid trumpet-tongued excess.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep musical elements moderate and fitting to the setting and audience size. As urban spectacle grew, music and choreography expanded—use such expansion with care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain dignity of tragic heroes (avoid buffoonery)
rubrics_metrics.description: In plays with serious heroes, do not stoop to low buffoonery; tragic figures should not exchange their dignity for clownish speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep register consistent: tragic heroes should remain elevated; avoid mixing tragic figures with the low comic language of clowns or buffoons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid staging scenes that shock belief and disgust
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not put on stage acts that shock belief—Medea shedding her children's blood, Atreus cooking human flesh, Philomel turning into a bird—these are better told than shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep certain horrific or supernatural transformations offstage and report them via speech when necessary; explicit staging can generate disgust and break audience credulity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blend instruction and pleasure but preserve usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet who 'mixing grave and gay, can teach / And yet give pleasure' wins both young and old; art must both instruct and delight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for didactic efficacy with entertainment value. While mixing tones can succeed, it must be handled skillfully to avoid incoherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be concise and measured in didactic or lecturing passages
rubrics_metrics.description: When you lecture, be concise: the soul takes in short maxims and retains them whole; pouring more than the vessel holds wastes it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor brevity and memorable aphorisms in moral or instructive passages. Avoid prolixity that dilutes effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plausibility and internal logic in fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep near to truth in a fictitious piece; don't treat belief as matter of caprice (e.g., if a child is made a vampire, it must not be alive when ripped up).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain internal consistency and plausible cause-effect within invented worlds. Violations of the implied rules of the story jar readers and should be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolerance for minor faults; intolerance for repeated errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Some faults may be forgiven (a blot or two) but repeated blunders by the same copyist or performer are intolerable and mark a dunce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow occasional slips in long works, but correct persistent mistakes. Repetition of the same defect (in wording or performance) undermines credibility and invites ridicule (example: Choerilus).

rubrics_metrics.name: Study models: learn from the Greeks
rubrics_metrics.description: Make Greece your model when you write; turn Greek volumes over day and night.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imitate and learn from established exemplars (Homer, Greek tragedians and comic poets) to acquire craftsmanship and taste before innovating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wisdom and life experience as foundation of poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: The secret of writing well lies in wisdom: study philosophy, life, duties, manners; comprehension of life supplies living words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acquire moral and civic knowledge and observe life closely; poetry grounded in real understanding of human duties and manners will have more truthful language and sentiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refinement: remove redundancy and harshness
rubrics_metrics.description: A good poet checks redundance, improves harshnesses by wise refinement, removes idle weeds; makes Rome's soil teem with genial produce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edit ruthlessly to eliminate redundant or awkward phrasing. Strive for fluency, limpid expression, and dignified turns of phrase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastery of metrics and technical skill
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand metrical feet and their use (e.g., the iambic foot definition and the trimeter's structure and spondaic substitutions); false rhythm may escape casual judges but marks lack of skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn technical prosody: where spondees may substitute, which places are fixed, and how metric choices affect the perceived smoothness and suitability of verse on stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize varied reception and cultivate durable excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Some works please at first glance, some only after repeated readings; middling poetry fails outright—aim for excellence rather than moderate merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand audience variation: some pieces need repeated exposure. Nevertheless, avoid middling work—better to strive for high quality than to be merely adequate.
